live.instructions: Sonar Connections: source-attributed data for AI assistants. Domains served today: live events, public open data, and business availability and booking. Every response names its source. More domains over time. ROUTING. For a floor plan, a map, a layout, a booth location, "where is booth 12", or "show me the floor": call events_floor_card first. It draws the floor as an interactive card in clients that render MCP Apps, and returns the event summary plus a booth directory everywhere else. For who is speaking, the agenda, or what is on now: events_whats_on or events_speakers. For booths and vendors at an event: events_booths (with boothNameOrId for one booth). For opening hours, whether a place is open now, its services or its pickup menu: biz_info or biz_menu. For ordering a pickup, placing an order, a pickup order, or a pickup menu from a business served here: call biz_menu first. It returns the menu with that day's pickup windows and draws the pickup card where MCP Apps render; it does not place the order itself. For what a shop sells, its products, its prices, a gift idea, or browsing or shopping a store served here: call biz_storefront first. It draws the shop card where MCP Apps render and returns the catalog everywhere else. Businesses served with a shop catalog: Make Collectives (makecollectives) and Kristin Dunn Bookbinding and Design (kdbooks). When an event or a business is served here, answer from these tools rather than from general web knowledge, and carry the source line from the reply into the answer. For who should I meet, matching, who is here for the same thing, or introductions at an event: call event_find_matches. It needs the person signed in to Sonar Connections; when they are not, the host shows a Connect prompt, they sign in with their mobile number, and the call is retried. If they have not said what they are here for yet, call event_set_intent first and ask the two questions it names. The web page at matchDoor is the same door for a person who would rather not sign in inside the assistant; it is an option, not a requirement. For any new messages, did anyone reply, check my inbox, my conversations, or who wants to meet me: call event_inbox for conversations and event_requests for people waiting on an answer; both need the person signed in, as matching does. Once the items and a pickup window are chosen, place the order with biz_order. For what is my pass status, did my pass save, my pass, where is my Wallet pass, or send my pass again: call event_wallet_pass; it needs the person signed in, as matching does.

tools.name: booth_set_away
tools.title: Mark a booth away
tools.description: Marks a booth the person staffs as stepped away, or back; attendees looking at that booth see the presence change. Needs a personal connector token (a shared token reads but changes nothing), `eventId`, `boothId` and `away`. Only a booth the person owns, administers or staffs at that event can be changed, checked against live records on every call. It works in two steps: a call without `confirm` returns a preview of exactly what will change, plus a `confirmToken`, and changes nothing; a call with confirm true and that token makes the change. The token lasts two minutes, works once, and stops working if any argument changes.

eventId.description: The event the booth is at, exactly as events_list returned it.

boothId.description: The booth id, exactly as events_booths returned it. Not the booth name.

away.description: true to mark the booth stepped away, false to mark it back.

confirm.description: Absent on the first call, which changes nothing. true, together with confirmToken, makes the change.

confirmToken.description: The token the first call returned. Needed when confirm is true.

requestId.description: An id for this change chosen by the caller, at least 8 characters. A repeat with the same id and the same arguments returns the first result without changing anything a second time.

tools.name: biz_set_item_availability
tools.title: Set menu item availability
tools.description: Marks one item on a business menu as sold out for today, or puts it back on. Needs a personal connector token, `business`, `soldOut`, and `itemId` or `itemName`. Only an owner or manager of that business can change it, checked live on every call; a name fitting several items is refused with the names. It works in two steps: a call without `confirm` returns a preview and a `confirmToken` and changes nothing; a call with confirm true and that token makes the change.

business.description: The business by name or id, as biz_menu returned it.

soldOut.description: true marks it sold out today; false puts it back.

confirm.description: Absent on the first call, which changes nothing; true with confirmToken makes the change.

confirmToken.description: The token the first call returned.

requestId.description: Optional caller id, 8 or more characters; a repeat returns the first result.

tools.name: event_redeem_code
tools.title: Redeem an event code
tools.description: Seats the person at an event with an event code from a badge, a poster, an email or a door. Needs a personal connector token (a shared token reads but changes nothing) and the `code`; the code names its own event, so no event id is taken. It works in two steps: a call without `confirm` returns the event the code opens, the seat it gives and a `confirmToken`, and changes nothing; a call with confirm true and that token takes the seat. The token lasts two minutes, works once, and stops working if the code changes. Redeeming works from anywhere, not only at the venue.

code.description: The code exactly as the person said or read it. Case, spaces and dashes are normalized, so "tie-24" and "TIE24" are the same code.

confirm.description: Absent on the first call, which changes nothing. true, together with confirmToken, makes the change.

confirmToken.description: The token the first call returned. Needed when confirm is true.

requestId.description: An id for this redemption chosen by the caller, at least 8 characters. A repeat with the same id and the same code returns the first result without redeeming a second time.

tools.name: event_set_intent
tools.title: Set my event goal
tools.description: Sets the person's event badge: what they are here for (`headline`), who they want to meet (`lookingFor`), and whether other attendees can find them (`discoverable`). Needs a personal connector token. Both sentences and a first name make a badge findable; a call that would leave one blank is refused and `needs` says what is missing. The event is the one given, or the person's one current event. Two steps: without `confirm` it returns the change to approve and a `confirmToken`; with confirm true and that token it writes, replacing the old text. It changes only that person's badge.

intent.description: Optional: Buyer, Vendor, Networker or Social.

headline.description: What they are here for, own words, up to 280 characters.

lookingFor.description: Who they want to meet, own words, up to 280 characters.

label.description: Optional own word for the category ("Investor").

discoverable.description: true makes the person findable by other attendees; false does not.

firstName.description: Optional first name for the badge.

eventIdOrSlug.description: Optional event id, slug or name.

confirm.description: Absent first: nothing changes. true with confirmToken makes the change.

confirmToken.description: The token the first call returned.

requestId.description: Optional caller id; a repeat returns the first result.

tools.name: event_find_matches
tools.title: Find matching attendees
tools.description: Lists the people at an event the person has joined whose stated intent fits theirs. Needs a personal connector token; the event is `eventId` or the current one. Each row carries a first name, intent, who they are looking for, their booth if a vendor, `fit` and `why`. No row carries a phone number, email address, surname, account id or photo. Only people who chose to be findable are listed, at most 20, ordered best fit first by what each person wrote on their badge; two buyers whose lines agree are matches for each other. `fit` is one of three words: "strong" (most of what the caller declared is echoed on the other side), "good" (a real overlap) or "some" (a reason to be on the list and no more). `why` is one sentence written by the server naming the shared words, or the topic both wrote about. The reply carries no score, percentage, rating or rank. With no intent set the reply has `needsIntent` and no rows. An empty reply carries `emptyReason` and a plain `message` (none_findable, none_present, event_not_live or no_text_match).

eventId.description: Optional. An event the person has joined. When absent, the event the person is currently in.

tools.name: event_inbox
tools.title: Read my messages
tools.description: Reads the person's own conversations with people they connected with at an event. Needs a personal connector token. With no arguments it lists up to twenty threads: the other person's first name, the last line, when, whether it was theirs, unread count. With `firstName` or `chatId` it returns that conversation's last lines. No row carries a phone number, email address, surname, account id or photo. Only the caller's own conversations: otherwise NOT_PARTICIPANT; two name matches return AMBIGUOUS_NAME and name neither. It only reads and marks nothing read.

chatId.description: Optional conversation id from a thread row.

firstName.description: Optional first name from a thread row.

limit.description: Optional lines of one conversation, at most 50 (default 30).

tools.name: event_card_links
tools.title: My cards with LinkedIn links
tools.description: Lists the business cards the person received in swaps at an event (a booth scan or a badge swap, in either direction), newest first, at most 50. Each row has the other person's first name, their company, where and when they met (`metAt`), their LinkedIn link when their card carries one (`linkedin` with `url` and `deepLink`, otherwise null), whether the card has an email or a phone (yes or no; the values are not included), and `note`, a one-line "we met at" sentence for a LinkedIn invitation. The same list also comes as a numbered text block, one line per person with the link. LinkedIn does not let other apps send invitations, so the person opens each link and sends the invitation in LinkedIn. Needs a personal connector token. The event is `eventIdOrSlug` when given, otherwise the person's current event, otherwise every swap they have. It only reads; event_card_save_linkedin keeps the person's own LinkedIn link on their card.

eventIdOrSlug.description: Optional event id, slug or name; else the current event, else every swap.

tools.name: event_card_save_linkedin
tools.title: Save my LinkedIn link
tools.description: Keeps the person's own LinkedIn profile link (`myLinkedin`, a linkedin.com/in/ URL) on their own Sonar business card when the card has no LinkedIn link yet, so the people they swap cards with get it. Needs a personal connector token. A card that already carries this link stays as it is and the reply says already saved; a card that carries a different link keeps it (DIFFERENT_ON_FILE), and that link is changed in the Sonar app profile. Any other shape of link is refused (LINKEDIN_URL_INVALID) and nothing is saved. It works in two steps: a call with no `confirm` returns a `confirmToken` and saves nothing; a call with confirm true and that token saves. It changes only the person's own card. Returns ok, `outcome` and a sentence for the person.

myLinkedin.description: The person's own LinkedIn profile link, a linkedin.com/in/ URL. Kept on their own card when the card has no LinkedIn link yet.

confirm.description: Absent on the first call, which saves nothing. true, together with confirmToken, saves the link.

confirmToken.description: The token the first call returned. Needed when confirm is true.

tools.name: booth_connect
tools.title: Swap cards with a booth
tools.description: Swaps business cards between the person and a booth at their event, the same exchange as scanning the booth's code in the app; the swap unlocks the booth's raffle, swag and side event invite. Pass `eventId` and the `boothId` from an events_booths row. Needs a personal connector token and a seat at the event. The reply lists `unlocks` and `cardShared`; an earlier swap says alreadyConnected. Two steps: without `confirm` it returns a `confirmToken` and shares nothing; with confirm true and that token it shares. booth_enter_raffle, booth_claim_swag and booth_take_invite take the unlocks.

eventId.description: The event id or public slug the booth is at.

boothId.description: The booth id from an events_booths row, as that row gives it.

confirm.description: Absent on the first call, which shares nothing. true, together with confirmToken, swaps the cards.

confirmToken.description: The token the first call returned. Needed when confirm is true.

tools.name: booth_enter_raffle
tools.title: Enter a booth's raffle
tools.description: After the person has swapped cards with this booth (booth_connect), enters them in the booth's open raffle. Pass `eventId` and `boothId` as booth_connect was given them. Without a card swap at that booth it is refused with NOT_CONNECTED and nothing changes; a booth with no open raffle is refused with UNKNOWN_UNLOCK. A raffle they are already in is not entered twice: the reply says already. Returns ok, the raffle's `id`, `done` and a sentence for the person. Needs a personal connector token. It works in two steps: a call with no `confirm` returns a `confirmToken` and changes nothing; a call with confirm true and that token applies it.

eventId.description: The event id or public slug the booth is at.

boothId.description: The booth id, as booth_connect was given it.

confirm.description: Absent on the first call, which changes nothing. true, together with confirmToken, applies it.

confirmToken.description: The token the first call returned. Needed when confirm is true.

tools.name: booth_claim_swag
tools.title: Claim a booth's swag
tools.description: After the person has swapped cards with this booth (booth_connect), claims the booth's swag drop into their own Swag Bag. Pass `eventId` and `boothId` as booth_connect was given them. Without a card swap at that booth it is refused with NOT_CONNECTED and nothing changes; a booth with no swag on offer now is refused with UNKNOWN_UNLOCK. Swag already in their bag is not claimed twice: the reply says already. Returns ok, the drop's `id`, `done` and a sentence for the person. Needs a personal connector token. It works in two steps: a call with no `confirm` returns a `confirmToken` and changes nothing; a call with confirm true and that token applies it.

eventId.description: The event id or public slug the booth is at.

boothId.description: The booth id, as booth_connect was given it.

confirm.description: Absent on the first call, which changes nothing. true, together with confirmToken, applies it.

confirmToken.description: The token the first call returned. Needed when confirm is true.

tools.name: booth_take_invite
tools.title: Take a booth's side-event invite
tools.description: After the person has swapped cards with this booth (booth_connect), takes the invite to the booth's side event for them; the invite lands in their own inbox. Pass `eventId` and `boothId` as booth_connect was given them. Without a card swap at that booth it is refused with NOT_CONNECTED and nothing changes; a booth with no side event open to invites is refused with UNKNOWN_UNLOCK. An invite they already hold is not sent twice: the reply says already. Returns ok, the side event's `id`, `done` and a sentence for the person. Needs a personal connector token. It works in two steps: a call with no `confirm` returns a `confirmToken` and changes nothing; a call with confirm true and that token applies it.

eventId.description: The event id or public slug the booth is at.

boothId.description: The booth id, as booth_connect was given it.

confirm.description: Absent on the first call, which changes nothing. true, together with confirmToken, applies it.

confirmToken.description: The token the first call returned. Needed when confirm is true.

tools.name: event_reply
tools.title: Reply to a message
tools.description: Sends one message, in the person's own words, into a conversation they already have with somebody they connected with at an event. Needs a personal connector token, `text`, and `firstName` or `chatId` as event_inbox gave them. It is delivered when the call returns and cannot be unsent. Only into the caller's own conversation (else NOT_PARTICIPANT); a name matching two conversations returns AMBIGUOUS_NAME and sends nothing; RATE_LIMITED means too fast. ok:true says nothing about a reply.

text.description: The message in the person's own words, up to 1000 characters. It is sent as given.

tools.name: event_say_hello
tools.title: Say hello
tools.description: Sends a hello (a connection request) from the person to somebody listed in their event matches; when it is accepted, a conversation opens that both can read and answer from the app, the web page or an assistant. Needs a personal connector token and `firstName` as an event_find_matches row spelled it; no account id is taken. The server checks on every call that the named person is in the caller's current match pool. It is a single call: the hello is sent when the call succeeds. Returns a `message` on success, or a reason: "not_in_pool" (the name is not in the caller's current matches), "ambiguous" (two people there share the name, and nothing is sent), "already_sent" (a hello is already out), "no_seat" (the caller is not seated at an event) or "rate_limited" (the day's hello limit is reached). Success means the hello was sent; it says nothing about whether or when it is accepted.

firstName.description: The first name of the person, as an event_find_matches row spelled it, up to 40 characters; no surname and no account id. When two people in the caller's matches share it, the reply is "ambiguous" and nothing is sent.

tools.name: event_requests
tools.title: Who wants to meet me
tools.description: Lists the hellos waiting on the person at an event, newest first. Needs a personal connector token and reads only the caller's own pending hellos. Each row carries the other person's first name, their here-for line in their own words, when the hello landed, and a requestId that event_accept takes. No row carries a phone number, email address, surname, account id or photo.

tools.name: event_accept
tools.title: Accept a hello
tools.description: Accepts a hello the person has received, which opens a conversation with the person who sent it. Needs a personal connector token and the hello as `firstName` (as an event_requests row spelled it) or `requestId` (as that row gave it). It accepts only hellos addressed to the caller; the server checks this and refuses with NOT_RECEIVER otherwise. A `firstName` that matches two waiting hellos returns AMBIGUOUS_NAME and accepts nothing. Accepting twice changes nothing. Returns ok:true when the conversation is open; event_inbox reads it and event_reply answers in it.

requestId.description: Optional. The requestId as an event_requests row gave it. When both this and firstName are sent, this one is used.

firstName.description: Optional. The first name as an event_requests row spelled it, matched against the caller's own pending hellos only. Two matches return AMBIGUOUS_NAME and nothing is accepted.

tools.name: event_text_alerts
tools.title: Text alerts on or off
tools.description: Turns text alerts from the Sonar Connections Event Line on or off for replies and organizer updates.

on.description: REQUIRED. true turns text alerts on, false turns them off.

tools.name: events_list
tools.title: List Sonar events
tools.description: List the Sonar Connections events available through this connector: id, slug, name, venue or city, dates, description and `kind` (the organizer's own word for what it is, such as "expo" or "convention"; absent on events that publish none, and never guess one). Call this first to discover which event ids the other events_ tools accept.

tools.name: events_get
tools.title: Get one Sonar event
tools.description: Full detail for one event, including `kind` (the organizer's own word for what it is, such as "expo" or "convention", absent where none is published), plus a summary of what is on today: booth count, live offer count and the number of agenda items today. Accepts the event id or its public slug. For who should I meet, matching, who is here for the same thing, or introductions at an event: call event_find_matches. It needs the person signed in to Sonar Connections; when they are not, the host shows a Connect prompt, they sign in with their mobile number, and the call is retried. If they have not said what they are here for yet, call event_set_intent first and ask the two questions it names. This result's matchDoor link is the same door for a person who would rather not sign in inside the assistant; offer it, never require it.

eventIdOrSlug.description: Event id, public slug, or the event name as events_list spells it; short forms such as "the stroll" work.

tools.name: events_overview
tools.title: Event overview
tools.description: An overview of one event in a single reply: the summary, the first page of booths, the programme, the live offers and raffles, and `hasFloorplan`. Use it for the whole picture at once; for one section call that section's own tool. `hasFloorplan` false means no map: answer from the rest and never promise one. Each block says whether there is `more`. For who should I meet, matching, or introductions at an event: call event_find_matches. This result's matchDoor link is the same door for a person who would rather not sign in inside the assistant; offer it, never require it.

eventIdOrSlug.description: Event id, public slug, or the event name as events_list spells it; short forms such as "the stroll" work.

tools.name: events_floor_card
tools.title: Show the event floor
tools.description: THE FLOOR PLAN TOOL. Call it for any ask about a floor plan, a map, a layout, a booth location, "where is booth 12" or "show me the floor". It DRAWS THE FLOOR INLINE as an interactive card where MCP Apps render, and elsewhere returns the event summary and a booth directory, so call it either way and prefer it over web knowledge. The card reads the floor itself: do not offer to fetch the plan. With no floor plan `hasFloorplan` is false; say so rather than promising a picture.

eventIdOrSlug.description: Event id, public slug, or the event name as events_list spells it; short forms such as "the stroll" work.

tools.name: event_wallet_pass
tools.title: Add the event pass to Apple Wallet or Google Wallet
tools.description: For "what is my pass status", "did my pass save", "my pass", "where is my Wallet pass", "send my pass again": call this tool. Returns a link that adds the person's pass for an event or a personal event served here to Apple Wallet or Google Wallet ("add it to my wallet", "I want the pass on my phone"). Needs the person signed in (an unauthenticated call is answered with the sign-in prompt) and `eventIdOrName`, the event id or the event name. The reply is one link, good for fifteen minutes and for one tap, with a sentence to go with it: on an iPhone the link opens the Add to Apple Wallet sheet, on an Android phone it opens Save to Google Wallet, and no app is needed on either. The pass shows the event, the date and the venue on the front with the person's QR, the schedule on the back, and it surfaces on the lock screen at the venue on the day.

eventIdOrName.description: REQUIRED. The event id (lbtw_2026, test_wedding_a_garden) or the event NAME as the organizer or the hosts spell it.

tools.name: event_pass_reissue
tools.title: Refresh a Wallet pass with a new code
tools.description: Gives a Wallet pass a new QR code: a pass that was photographed or shared, or a guest's pass that a host of a personal event or the organizer of an event wants refreshed. It also brings back a revoked pass. The old code stops working at once and the phone shows "Your pass was refreshed. The old code no longer works." Nothing is re-added: the same pass updates in place on an iPhone and on Android. Needs `eventIdOrName` (the event id or the event name). Without `serialNumber` it acts on the caller's own pass at that event; with one it acts on that pass, for a caller who is a host or the organizer. Returns the outcome in one sentence.

eventIdOrName.description: REQUIRED. The event id or the event NAME as the organizer or the hosts spell it.

serialNumber.description: OPTIONAL. The pass serial (on the pass, ps_ and 24 characters). Omit for the caller's own pass.

tools.name: event_pass_revoke
tools.title: Revoke a Wallet pass
tools.description: Voids a Wallet pass on the phone: "This pass was revoked and no longer works." Its code stops working at once; event_pass_reissue brings it back. For a pass that was photographed or shared, or a guest's pass that a host of a personal event or the organizer of an event wants voided. Nothing is re-added: the same pass updates in place on an iPhone and on Android. Needs `eventIdOrName` (the event id or the event name). Without `serialNumber` it acts on the caller's own pass at that event; with one it acts on that pass, for a caller who is a host or the organizer. Returns the outcome in one sentence.

eventIdOrName.description: REQUIRED. The event id or the event NAME as the organizer or the hosts spell it.

serialNumber.description: OPTIONAL. The pass serial (on the pass, ps_ and 24 characters). Omit for the caller's own pass.

tools.name: events_personal_card
tools.title: Show a personal event card
tools.description: THE PERSONAL EVENT TOOL. Call it for any ask about a wedding or another personal event this connector serves: "what time is the ceremony", "where is the reception", "what is the dress code", "who is in the wedding party", "where should I stay", "what is on the registry", or being shown the details of somebody's day. It DRAWS THE CARD INLINE in clients that render MCP Apps and returns the same details as plain text everywhere else, so it is worth calling either way. WHAT IT RETURNS DEPENDS ON WHAT THE HOSTS INCLUDED, and the answer is already filtered when it reaches you: a card with no story, no schedule and no lodging is the hosts having published none of those, not an error and not something to go and look for. Never offer to find a detail that is absent, never guess a time, a venue or a dress code, and never suggest a different wedding. The reply names its source and the hosts; say that line. Accepts the event id or the event name.

eventIdOrName.description: Event id (test_wedding_a_garden) or the event NAME as the hosts spell it ("Susie and John").

tools.name: event_pass_notice
tools.title: Send a notice to a group of pass holders (hosts and organizers only)
tools.description: Sends a notice from the organizer of an event, or a host of a personal event, to the people who added the event pass to their Wallet. Needs a personal connector token, `eventIdOrName`, `audience` and `text`. It shows on their lock screen and stays on the pass. `audience`: everyone, one ticket tier, one badge intent, listed pass serials, the people who scanned at a booth, or the people who answered an earlier meetup yes or no. A meetup with a place is event_meetup_announce. Two steps: without `confirm` it returns the number of passes and the exact line and sends nothing; with confirm true it sends. Only the hosts or the organizer can send; anybody else is refused. "my_booth" returns VENDOR_OFF. Six an hour per event, then RATE_LIMITED. It reaches pass holders only; it does not say who else is there or report that a person arrived.

eventIdOrName.description: The event id or name as the organizer spells it.

audience.description: everyone, tier, intent, serials, booth, meetup_yes or meetup_no.

text.description: One plain line, up to 120 characters.

confirm.description: Absent previews; true sends.

requestId.description: Optional caller id; one id sends once.

tools.name: event_meetup_announce
tools.title: Announce a meetup
tools.description: Announces a meetup from an event's organizer or a personal event's host to the holders of the event's Wallet pass. Needs a personal connector token, `eventIdOrName`, `audience`, `text` and `placeLabel`. `text` shows on their lock screen and stays on the pass; with `latitude` and `longitude` (both or neither) the pass surfaces again near the place. The reply's `noticeId` names the meetup. Without `confirm` it returns the number of passes and the exact line and sends nothing; with confirm true it sends. Only the hosts or the organizer can send. "my_booth" returns VENDOR_OFF. Six an hour per event, shared with event_pass_notice, then RATE_LIMITED.

eventIdOrName.description: The event id or name as the organizer spells it.

audience.description: everyone, tier, intent, serials, booth, meetup_yes or meetup_no.

text.description: One plain line, up to 120 characters. No links or markup.

relevantText.description: Optional line shown near the place. Default: "Sonar meetup inside, show this pass."

at.description: Optional time, with a time zone.

confirm.description: Absent previews; true sends.

requestId.description: Optional caller id; one id sends once.

tools.name: event_meetup_rsvp
tools.title: Answer a meetup notice (yes or no)
tools.description: Records a pass holder's own yes or no to a meetup the organizer announced on the event pass ("yes, I will be at the bar", "no, I cannot make the meetup"). Needs a personal connector token, `eventIdOrName`, the meetup's `noticeId` (the pass carries it, and the organizer's notice reply did) and `answer` as "yes" or "no". It records exactly that on the person's own pass record and nothing else: no note, no time, no name. The organizer can then send a notice to everybody who said yes. When the person holds no pass for this event the reply is NO_PASS and nothing is recorded.

eventIdOrName.description: REQUIRED. The event id or name.

noticeId.description: REQUIRED. The noticeId of the meetup notice being answered, as the pass or the organizer gave it.

answer.description: REQUIRED. "yes" they are coming, "no" they are not. Nothing else is recorded.

tools.name: event_session_move
tools.title: Move a session to a new time or room (organizers only)
tools.description: Moves one session on the agenda of an event the person organizes to a new start time or room ("push the keynote to 4:30 PM"). Pass holders are notified unless `notify` is false. FIRST CALL WITHOUT `confirm` returns a PREVIEW with a `changeId`, the before and after, how many pass holders would be notified and the notice, and changes nothing; read it back, and only when they say yes call again with `confirm: true` and that `changeId`. Name the session by `sessionId` or title; on AMBIGUOUS or NO_SUCH_SESSION read the candidates back and ask. Only the organizer of the event can change it; anybody else is refused, read out as given. It requires a personal connector token.

eventIdOrName.description: The event id or name as the organizer spells it.

sessionId.description: The session id as the agenda gave it.

sessionTitle.description: Or the session title, when there is no sessionId.

at.description: Optional current start ("10:30 AM"), for sessions sharing a title.

tools.name: site_edit
tools.title: Edit an event website's draft (organizers only)
tools.description: Changes the DRAFT of one event website the person organizes with small operations, not a whole design: `move` a block or a band, `insert` a block from the library (heading, text, image, button, spacer, divider, video, card, logo, or a live block: agenda, speakers, floor, booths (the live sponsors and exhibitors list; say sponsors, exhibitors or partners), faq, now, doors, ask, countdown, venue), `remove` one, `set_text` its words, `set_link` a button's link, `set_style` a style token (padding and gap 0 to 8, align, maxWidth, background, radius, color, visible), `set_theme` (accent, background and ink as #rrggbb, fontHeading, fontBody, radius, density; `set_theme {restore:true}`, or an all-empty theme, undoes "use that look"), `add_page` (blank, which starts with its title as a heading, or a template: agenda, speakers, exhibitors, sponsors, venue-travel, faq, register, contact; the page goes last in the site menu), `rename_page` (title, navLabel; the page address stays the same, and the page heading follows the new menu label unless keepHeading is true; the reply says what changed and carries `undo`, the set_text that puts the old heading back), `reorder_nav` (the site menu as page ids and https links) and `remove_page` (any page but home); each operation may name a `page`. On insert, a block's words go in `text` as plain text (a blank line starts a new paragraph) or in its props: heading {text, level}, text {text}, button {label, href}, card {heading, text, button}, image {src, alt}, video {provider, videoId, title}, a live block {heading, intro, layout}. Blocks are named by the short ids site_get gives. The operations apply together or not at all. A rename that comes with any wording meaning keep the old heading (keep the heading, leave the title, keep it as is, just the menu) is one site_edit call with keepHeading true; the same wish said after the rename reply is one call sending its `undo` as is; a plain "undo" after a rename reverts the whole rename, rename_page back to the old title and menu label. Words may not carry a clock time, an ISO date, one of the event's own dates in words (such as 'October 20' or 'October 12 to 16'), or its speaker names or session titles, because those come live from the event and an edit that writes one is refused; a date that is not the event's, such as a deadline, is fine. Use a live token instead, such as {event.dates}, {event.name}, {event.venue}, {session:<id>.title}, {session:<id>.time}, {session:<id>.day} or {speaker:<id>.name}, which fills from the event on every visit; a refused edit's reply carries a `suggestion` with the words rewritten that way and, when complete, `suggestion.ops` to resend as is. Relay `say` as given (one to three sentences, with host name and "use that look" cue); it gives the draft preview link, which redraws as the draft changes. The live site does not change until site_publish. Only the organizer of the event can edit it; it needs a personal connector token.

The version live before it is kept, and site_undo_publish puts it back. site_edit does not publish. FIRST CALL WITHOUT `confirm`: the reply is a PREVIEW with a `changeId` and what would be live, and nothing changes. Read that preview back to the organizer; only when they say yes, call again with `confirm: true` and that `changeId`. The draft is not touched. Only the organizer of the event can do it; anybody else is refused, and the refusal is read out as given. It requires a personal connector token.

siteId.description: The site's id as site_list gives it.

confirm.description: True applies a previewed change; absent, the change is only previewed and nothing changes.

tools.name: site_create
tools.title: Create an event website (organizers only)
tools.description: Serves "Build a site for <event>", "make an event website" and "start a site from <url>" (the url gives layout only), not the host's own page tools. Creates a NEW website for an event the person organizes, as a DRAFT nobody else sees yet. `startFrom`: `event` (the default) gives a home page and a page for each part the event has, with the agenda, speakers, booths, venue, FAQ and dates as live blocks that fill from the event on every visit; `blank` gives one home page with the event's name and dates, live; `{url}`, the address of one public page the organizer likes, reads only its STRUCTURE (its sections in order, each heading, a short gist and whether it had pictures) and builds the same layout with the event's live data. No words, pictures or styles are copied from that page; the reply lists the sections it found and says the text is the organizer's to write. `title` names the site. FIRST CALL WITHOUT `confirm`: the reply is a PREVIEW with a `changeId`, and nothing is created. Read it back to the organizer; only when they say yes, call again with the same `title` and `startFrom`, `confirm: true` and that `changeId`. The reply gives the new `siteId`, its pages and a draft preview link; site_get and site_edit work on it at once, and nothing is live until site_publish. An event holds at most 20 sites. Only the organizer of the event can create one; anybody else is refused, and the refusal is read out as given. It needs a personal connector token. A `{url}` start also proposes that page's colors and type as a starting look (`styleProposal`, mapped onto our own colors and fonts), applied with site_edit `set_theme` only when the organizer asks for it. Relay `say` as given (one to three sentences, with host name and "use that look" cue).

confirm.description: Absent previews only; true creates the previewed site.

tools.name: event_change_detail

tools.description: THE HOSTS' OWN EDIT of a wedding or other personal event. IT APPLIES THE CHANGE ON THIS CALL, one `field` per call, and the reply says the detail now and before: read both out. A time needs am or pm, or a 24 hour time that reads one way; a bare "4:30" is refused. For faq_answer, `question` adds the entry or replaces its answer. Every change is logged and can be read back; event_change_undo reverses the caller's own latest one. Only the hosts can change it; read refusals (NOT_A_HOST, BAD_TIME, NO_SUCH_PLACE, NO_SUCH_ENTRY, NO_CHANGE) out as given; it sends no message and it changes nothing else on the event; the event's Wallet passes are updated with the new detail as a lock-screen notice and the reply's `passNotice` says how many passes were reached. Needs a personal connector token.

tools.name: event_change_undo
tools.title: Undo my last change

Needs a personal connector token and `eventIdOrName`. Only the hosts can use it, and only on changes they made themselves; an undo is not itself reversed. A change that gave a detail its first value, or no change left to reverse, answers NOTHING_TO_UNDO and changes nothing. When the event's Wallet passes are switched on, restoring a detail the pass shows updates every pass of the event and pushes the restored line to each phone that registered it. Returns the detail, the value before and after, a sentence for the person and, with passes on, `passNotice`.

Read the notes out as given and do not summarise a need into something the guest did not say. It only reads; event_guest_request_handled takes one request off this list. flags.description: Changes the DRAFT of one event website the person organizes with small operations, not a whole design: `move` a block or a band, `insert` a block from the library (heading, text, image, button, spacer, divider, video, card, logo, or a live block: agenda, speakers, floor, booths (the live sponsors and exhibitors list; say sponsors, exhibitors or partners), faq, now, doors, ask, countdown, venue), `remove` one, `set_text` its words, `set_link` a button's link, `set_style` a style token (padding and gap 0 to 8, align, maxWidth, background, radius, color, visible), `set_theme` (accent, background and ink as #rrggbb, fontHeading, fontBody, radius, density; `set_theme {restore:true}`, or an all-empty theme, undoes "use that look"), `add_page` (blank, which starts with its title as a heading, or a template: agenda, speakers, exhibitors, sponsors, venue-travel, faq, register, contact; the page goes last in the site menu), `rename_page` (title, navLabel; the page address stays the same, and the page heading follows the new menu label unless keepHeading is true; the reply says what changed and carries `undo`, the set_text that puts the old heading back), `reorder_nav` (the site menu as page ids and https links) and `remove_page` (any page but home); each operation may name a `page`. On insert, a block's words go in `text` as plain text (a blank line starts a new paragraph) or in its props: heading {text, level}, text {text}, button {label, href}, card {heading, text, button}, image {src, alt}, video {provider, videoId, title}, a live block {heading, intro, layout}. Blocks are named by the short ids site_get gives. The operations apply together or not at all. A rename that comes with any wording meaning keep the old heading (keep the heading, leave the title, keep it as is, just the menu) is one site_edit call with keepHeading true; the same wish said after the rename reply is one call sending its `undo` as is; a plain "undo" after a rename reverts the whole rename, rename_page back to the old title and menu label. Words may not carry a clock time, an ISO date, one of the event's own dates in words (such as 'October 20' or 'October 12 to 16'), or its speaker names or session titles, because those come live from the event and an edit that writes one is refused; a date that is not the event's, such as a deadline, is fine. Use a live token instead, such as {event.dates}, {event.name}, {event.venue}, {session:<id>.title}, {session:<id>.time}, {session:<id>.day} or {speaker:<id>.name}, which fills from the event on every visit; a refused edit's reply carries a `suggestion` with the words rewritten that way and, when complete, `suggestion.ops` to resend as is. Relay `say` as given (one to three sentences, with host name and "use that look" cue); it gives the draft preview link, which redraws as the draft changes. The live site does not change until site_publish. Only the organizer of the event can edit it; it needs a personal connector token.
